definitions.explanation: Complete absence of light; extremely dark.
Figuratively, a situation with no hope or prospect of improvement.

examples.japanese: {停電|ていでん}で{部屋|へや}が{真|ま}っ{暗|くら}になった。
examples.english: The room went pitch dark due to the power outage.

examples.japanese: {将来|しょうらい}が{真|ま}っ{暗|くら}に{見|み}える。
{真|ま}っ{暗|くら}な{夜道|よみち}を{一人|ひとり}で{歩|ある}くのは{怖|こわ}い。
examples.english: It's scary to walk alone on a pitch-dark road at night.

notes:
WORD STRUCTURE:
{真|ま}っ (emphatic prefix) + {暗|くら}い (dark) → {暗|くら}

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
・{先行|さきゆ}きが{真|ま}っ{暗|くら} - the outlook is bleak
・{真|ま}っ{暗|くら}{闇|やみ} - complete darkness
・{目|め}の{前|まえ}が{真|ま}っ{暗|くら}になる - to black out; to despair

FIGURATIVE USAGE:
When used figuratively, {真|ま}っ{暗|くら} describes a hopeless situation where one cannot see any positive future.

RELATED:
・{真|ま}っ{黒|くろ} - pitch black (color)
・{暗闇|くらやみ} - darkness
・お{先|さき}{真|ま}っ{暗|くら} - bleak future (expression)
